content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any project documents relevant to absorber geometry, residual dose/radiation safety, and simulation assumptions. Extract the three allowed absorber materials, the applicable residual dose rate at 1 m after one week of cooldown, and any stated constraints or recommendations on plate thickness."},{"id":"s2","description":"From the documents, determine which materials and thickness ranges satisfy the hard residual dose limit of 20 uSv/h at 1 m after one week of cooldown. Exclude any material or thickness range that violates the dose limit. Record the relevant numeric dose values using record_results."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every dose-compliant material, run simulate_resolution for 100 GeV electrons at plate thicknesses 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 mm. Record every numeric resolution result using record_results, and identify all combinations with resolution <= 4.5%."},{"id":"s4","description":"Refine the search around the best-performing simulated thickness for each dose-compliant material by running simulate_resolution at 0.5 mm intervals within +/- 1 mm of that best thickness, bounded by 2 to 10 mm. Record all numeric resolution results using record_results."},{"id":"s5","description":"Select the feasible absorber design with the lowest simulated 100 GeV energy resolution among combinations satisfying both hard requirements: resolution <= 4.5% and residual dose <= 20 uSv/h. If no simulated combination satisfies both requirements, report that no feasible design was found rather than recommending a noncompliant option."}]}
